extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters who write local/city news
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and writing miscellaneous local (city) news: what to cover, two purposes of such stories, and the reporter skills and sources needed to produce timely, significant, or entertaining local items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources: public institutions and city departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Much interesting, timely information is to be found in schools, public Ubraries, museums, parks, and various departments of city government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are activities supported by public money and therefore should be of interest to every citizen; reporters should routinely monitor these institutions for timely items and developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business and economic local news
rubrics_metrics.description: Real estate, building, manufacturing, and business matters also furnish news of considerable interest and importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat business and economic developments as a key source of local news; these items often have broader civic importance and should be covered with attention to factual significance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal/entertaining city sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many little incidents in the daily hfe of every city that have no significance as news but that can be written up as entertaining stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pieces aim to entertain the reader with 'little glimpses of the life of the city.' Use vivid detail and narrative skill to turn small incidents into readable sketches even when they lack hard public significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venues for human-interest incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Hotels, railroad stations, docks, and street cars are frequently the scenes of little comedies and tragedies that the reporter... turns into readable sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should watch these public, transit, and travel spaces for human-interest moments and be ready to capture dialogue, action, and sensory detail that make short features compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals as central figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals no less than persons may be the central figures in these stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't dismiss animal incidents; they can provide strong human-interest hooks and vivid narrative material for local features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two classes of miscellaneous local stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in one class of these local stories is to furnish timely, significant information in attractive form concerning public institutions and business activities. The purpose of the other class is to entertain the reader with little glimpses of the life of the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning or writing such items, decide which class the piece belongs to (informative vs. entertaining) and shape tone, structure, and sourcing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — furnish timely, significant information attractively
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim ... is to furnish timely, significant information in attractive form concerning public institutions and business activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize timeliness and significance for this class; present facts clearly and attractively to engage citizens about municipal affairs and publicly funded institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — entertain with city-life glimpses
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the other class is to entertain the reader with little glimpses of the life of the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative devices, characterization, and evocative detail to create readable, entertaining vignettes; these pieces may sacrifice 'hard' news value for human interest and color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive journalism objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journaUsm undertakes to stimulate the interest of every citizen in municipal affairs and in public institutions by putting prominently before him from time to time significant information about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should aim not merely to inform but to engage citizens about public institutions — highlight relevance, context, and implications so readers understand why local matters matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter skill — insight and portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporter with keen insight into human life and with ability to portray them, turns [incidents] into readable sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop observational acuity, empathy, and descriptive writing skills; effective local features rely on the reporter's ability to interpret behavior and present it vividly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and significance as selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Much interesting, timely information ... and ... news of considerable interest and importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting local items, evaluate both timeliness (is it current?) and significance (does it affect or interest citizens?), and choose the appropriate treatment (informative or entertaining).
